newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE ENGLISH LEAGUE AND CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE ENGLISH LEAGUE AND CUP.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league and F.A. Cup semifinals (kick-off times 1400 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Premier League
Arsenal (2) v. Leicester (11)

Arsenal have forced their way back into the title chase after four wins in their last five games. Defender Remi Garde, who played in the 3-0 victory at Chelsea last Saturday, is expected to continue in place of ankle injury victim Tony Adams.
Leicester may be distracted by their League Cup final replay next Wednesday after a 1-1 draw at Wembley on Sunday.
Blackburn (13) v. Manchester United (1)

United, who lost 1-0 to Borussia Dortmund on Wednesday in the European Cup, need to reassert their title challenge after a 3-2 home defeat by Derby last Saturday. Coach Alex Ferguson has injury worries over Denis Irwin, Ryan Giggs and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer while Danish goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel and defender David May are out.
Blackburn, still in need of points to assure them of safety, have midfielder Tim Sherwood back after suspension.
Derby (12) v. Aston Villa (4)
Both sides have shown recent good form with Derby virtually safe in mid-table and Villa odds-on for a UEFA Cup place.

Derby will be without recent Estonian signing Mart Poom (shoulder) in goal and it is feared both he and Croatian defender Igor Stimac (back) could be out for the rest of the season. Veteran defender Paul McGrath returns after being rested.
Villa coach Brian Little is unlikely to change the team that won 2-0 at Wimbledon in midweek.
Everton (14) v. Tottenham (9)

Everton caretaker player/coach Dave Watson will be without midfielder Joe Parkinson, who suffered a knee injury in the 1-1 draw with Leicester on Wednesday. Points would be welcome for a side still not safe from relegation after just two wins in their last 16 league games.
Tottenham coach Gerry Francis has mounting injury problems with Danish midfielder Allan Nielsen the latest absentee. Swiss defender Ramon Vega could return.
Southampton (19) v. West Ham (16)
Southampton coach Graeme Souness, whose side have gone three games unbeaten, has the dilemma of whether to risk hamstring victim Matt Le Tissier for a relegation duel Saints must win.
Injury-hit West Ham welcome back defender Julian Dicks after a one-match ban as they look to extend a run of five games without loss.
Sheffield Wednesday (6) v. Newcastle (5) (Sunday 1400 GMT)
Sheffield Wednesday, with just one league defeat at home, face Newcastle with both sides aiming for a UEFA Cup place. Coach David Pleat is likely to recall defender Dejan Stefanovic.
Newcastle will give England striker Les Ferdinand a late fitness test on an injured shoulder, while Belgian defender Philippe Albert is out with a knee injury.
Sunderland (17) v. Liverpool (3) (Sunday 1400 GMT)

Liverpool suffered a demoralising 3-0 Cup Winners' Cup defeat at Paris St. Germain on Thursday to follow last week's 2-1 home reverse against Coventry. Coach Roy Evans has no injury worries but needs to rejuvenate his troops.
Sunderland, fighting relegation, gained their fifth point in three games with a 1-1 draw at Newcastle last Saturday and welcome back midfielder Michael Gray.
FA CUP SEMIFINALS
Middlesbrough v. Chesterfield OLD TRAFFORD (Sunday 1400 GMT)
Premier league Middlesbrough, aiming to reach their second cup final this season, are without cup-tied goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer and midfielder Phil Stamp. Defender Neil Cox returns after suspension.
Second division Chesterfield will give late fitness tests to goalkeeper Billy Mercer and defender Darren Carr after resting a number of players in midweek.
Wimbledon v. Chelsea HIGHBURY (Sunday 1100 GMT)
Both sides go into the game out of form -- Wimbledon have not won a league game in eight outings and Chelsea have lost their last three.

Wimbledon coach Joe Kinnear is set to recall eight first team members rested for the midweek defeat by Aston Villa and Chelsea coach Ruud Gullit's only major doubt is ankle injury victim striker Mark Hughes.
